properties.decision: Anthony, 2026-09-05: yes. The five dead /tmp exports cost every loop_status ~3.5 s because sync_debt re-reads and re-parses each target on every call to produce the in-step node count. The fix is NOT a rule about where files live - chg:the-orientation-call-stops-rereading-stale-records tried a /tmp rule and reverted it against fifteen correct tests, because hermetic tests, CI and containers all put genuine shared records under a temp dir. The fix is that an UNCHANGED file is not re-parsed: the sync record already stores each target's content hash; it will also store the node count observed at that hash, and a target whose current hash matches the recorded one reuses the count without parsing. A dead file never changes, so it is parsed once and never again; a live record that moved is parsed exactly as today. No target is dropped, no policy about paths is introduced, and the not_checked disclosure stays as it is. To be MEASURED before building: the 3.6 s is more than parse plus hash should cost (python parse of all six was 1.5 s), so the cost inside sync_debt is to be timed first - the fix must be aimed at what is actually slow.
properties.name: DECIDED - a sync target whose content has not changed is not re-parsed; its recorded node count is reused
properties.rationale: Chosen over 'read only targets newer than the committed record' (a policy that can silently skip a real collaborator's record) and over an explicit forget verb (which puts the burden on the user for a cost the tool created). Reusing a recorded count for an unchanged hash is a pure cache of a derived fact over immutable content and cannot change what is reported.
